messages.name: Emma Clarke
messages.body: Please help - water is POURING through my bathroom ceiling right now. It started about ten minutes ago and it's coming through around the light fitting. I've put the washing up bowl under it but it's filling fast. I don't know what to do, I have to leave for work at half eight.

messages.name: Dwelly Property Team
messages.body: Emma, we're treating this as an emergency. Please switch off the bathroom light at the fuse box and don't touch the fitting - water and electrics together are dangerous. We're calling the upstairs flat now to get their water shut off and getting a plumber out to you as a priority. Stay put if you possibly can.

messages.name: Emma Clarke
messages.body: Okay, light is off at the box. The flow has slowed a little but the ceiling is bulging near the corner and there's a long wet streak down the wall. I've called work to say I'll be late. Please hurry.

messages.name: Dwelly Property Team
messages.body: FlowFix Plumbing are on their way to you now, should be with you before 9. The upstairs neighbour has shut off their stopcock so the flow should keep easing. The plumber will need access to both flats - we've arranged entry upstairs already.

messages.name: Dan Whitfield (FlowFix Plumbing Ltd)
messages.body: On site. Found it - the cold feed to the upstairs bath has split inside the boxing, been spraying into the void over your ceiling. I've isolated it and the water's stopped. To repair the pipe, open up and dry the void, and make good the ceiling section it's £310 all in. Can start straight away if approved.

messages.name: Dwelly Property Team
messages.body: Spoke with Mr Hughes by phone just now - he's approved the £310 given there's active water damage to two flats. Dan, please go ahead immediately.

messages.name: Dan Whitfield (FlowFix Plumbing Ltd)
messages.body: Pipe replaced and pressure tested, no further leaks. I've cut back the damaged ceiling section and left an air mover running in the void - will collect it tomorrow and check moisture readings before the ceiling is patched. Light fitting checked and dried, safe to switch back on this evening.

messages.name: Emma Clarke
messages.body: Thank you both for moving so fast, honestly. Ceiling looks awful but everything is dry and the light works. The plumber was really good about explaining what happened.

classification.rationale: Active water ingress through a ceiling near electrics, affecting two flats.

resolution.summary: Split cold feed in upstairs boxing repaired and pressure tested same morning; void dried and ceiling section made good the following day. Landlord approved £310 by phone during the incident.

messages.name: Priya Shah
messages.body: Hi, the kitchen tap has started dripping and it's surprisingly loud at night - I can hear it from the bedroom with the door shut. It's maybe a drip every couple of seconds. Not urgent exactly but it's driving me a bit mad and I assume it's wasting water too.

messages.name: Dwelly Property Team
messages.body: Morning Priya, thanks for flagging it. A dripping tap is usually a worn cartridge or washer - quick fix, nothing alarming. We'll book Thames & Vale Plumbing in for you this week. In the meantime a rubber band tied round the spout so the drip runs down a string into the sink is the classic trick for the noise, if you're desperate.

messages.name: Thames & Vale Plumbing
messages.body: Hello, Thames & Vale here. We can do Thursday the 18th between 12 and 2pm for the tap at Beckford Lane. Someone will need to be in to give access to the kitchen. Reply to confirm and we'll lock it in.

messages.name: Priya Shah
messages.body: Thursday 12-2 works, I'm working from home that day. And the string trick actually works, who knew. See you Thursday.

messages.name: Thames & Vale Plumbing
messages.body: Job done - replaced the ceramic cartridge in the mixer and re-seated the spout O-ring while we were in there. Tap is drip-free and the handle feels less stiff too. Invoice for £85 going to Dwelly as usual.

classification.rationale: Minor plumbing fault, no water damage risk, routine appointment appropriate.

resolution.summary: Worn ceramic cartridge replaced in kitchen mixer tap during a routine Thursday slot; drip resolved, £85.

cases.title: Scuff marks and hairline crack in hallway paint

messages.name: Oliver Grant
messages.body: Hi, just wanted to log this rather than it being a surprise at checkout - there are some scuff marks along the hallway wall from when we moved the sofa in, and I've noticed a hairline crack in the paint above the kitchen door frame. Neither is getting worse as far as I can tell, just cosmetic.

messages.name: Dwelly Property Team
messages.body: Thanks Oliver, appreciated - always better to have these on record. Could you send a couple of photos of the crack above the door frame? Hairline cracks over doorways are almost always settlement in the plaster skim, but a photo lets us rule out anything structural.

messages.name: Oliver Grant
messages.body: Photos attached. The crack is about 15cm, thin as a pencil line, follows the top corner of the frame. The scuffs are just paint transfer really, some might come off with a magic eraser - I'll have a go myself.

messages.name: Dwelly Property Team
messages.body: That's classic skim settlement - nothing structural, no action needed now. We've logged both items against the property for the next redecoration cycle, so they'll be dealt with when the hallway is repainted rather than sending a decorator out for this alone. Closing this one off, and thanks again for the photos.

classification.rationale: Cosmetic only, no deterioration risk, fold into the planned redecoration cycle.

resolution.summary: Confirmed cosmetic (plaster skim settlement and scuffs); logged against the property for the next redecoration cycle, no contractor callout raised.

cases.title: Tiny leak under the sink, no rush

messages.name: Hannah Osei
messages.body: Morning! Nothing dramatic - there's a tiny leak under the kitchen sink. I noticed a damp patch on the cabinet floor yesterday and put a takeaway tub under the pipe. It catches maybe a teaspoon a day. No rush at all, whenever someone is next in the area.

messages.name: Dwelly Property Team
messages.body: Thanks Hannah. Just to gauge it - is the drip coming from a joint on the curved trap pipe, or higher up near the tap connections? And is the cabinet floor itself swollen or just damp on the surface?

messages.name: Hannah Osei
messages.body: It looks like it's from the joint where the curved bit meets the straight pipe going into the wall. Cabinet floor is just surface-damp, wiped it dry this morning and it's fine. Honestly it's a dribble.

messages.name: Dwelly Property Team
messages.body: Understood - we'll log this as medium priority and get a plumber out to you within the week. Keep the tub under it and give it a wipe when you think of it. If it visibly speeds up, let us know straight away.

messages.name: Hannah Osei
messages.body: Quick update - it's dripping a bit faster now, the tub was about a third full this morning rather than a puddle at the bottom. Still not scary but thought you should know. Any word on the plumber?

messages.name: Dwelly Property Team
messages.body: Thanks for the update - we're holding a slot with the plumber for Friday morning, will confirm the time window tomorrow. Apologies it wasn't sooner in the week; keep emptying the tub in the meantime.

messages.name: Jamal Reid (Flat 2, downstairs)
messages.body: Hi, I'm in Flat 2 directly below Flat 3. There's a brown stain on my kitchen ceiling that wasn't there at the weekend, and it's grown since yesterday - it's about the size of a dinner plate now and the paint is starting to bubble at one edge. I think water is coming from upstairs.

messages.name: Dwelly Property Team
messages.body: Jamal, thank you - that changes things. Hannah, the water from that joint has clearly been tracking down into the ceiling void rather than all landing in your tub, so this is now high priority and Friday is too late. We're pulling FlowFix in today. Hannah, please avoid running the kitchen tap until they've been.

messages.name: Dan Whitfield (FlowFix Plumbing Ltd)
messages.body: Attended Flat 3. The compression joint on the waste was barely finger-tight and the seal has perished - most of the escape was running down the back of the pipe into the floor void, which is why the tub stayed nearly empty. To replace the trap and waste run, dry the void, and check and treat the ceiling in Flat 2 it's £270 all in.

messages.name: Dwelly Property Team
messages.body: Quote of £270 sent over to Ms Whitlow for approval with photos of the Flat 2 ceiling - will revert as soon as we hear back.

messages.name: Margaret Whitlow
messages.body: Approved - please proceed today. Frustrating that a teaspoon a day turned into a neighbour's ceiling; let's not sit on leaks in future, even small ones.

messages.name: Dan Whitfield (FlowFix Plumbing Ltd)
messages.body: Done. New trap and waste fitted and tested, void dried with an air mover, moisture readings in the Flat 2 ceiling are borderline so I've left the mover running down there overnight. The stain will need a coat of stain-block and paint once fully dry - a decorator job, not plumbing.

messages.name: Hannah Osei
messages.body: All dry under the sink and honestly it looks tidier than before. Really sorry Jamal - I had no idea it was going through the floor. Thanks for sorting it so fast once it blew up.

messages.name: Dwelly Property Team
messages.body: Closing this off. Plumbing repair complete and tested; we've booked a decorator to stain-block and repaint the Flat 2 ceiling patch next week under a separate job. Jamal, they'll contact you directly to arrange access.

classification.rationale: Water escape reached the flat below - active ingress affecting another unit.

resolution.summary: Perished waste joint under the sink replaced and tested after the leak tracked into the ceiling of the flat below; voids dried, £270 approved by landlord, ceiling redecoration raised separately.

property.address: Ashcombe House, 3 Pelham Street, London SW7 2NB

cases.title: Smell of gas in the entrance hall

messages.name: Nadia Ferreira
messages.body: Hi - there's a strong smell of gas in the entrance hall of the building. I noticed it as soon as I came in from work just now. It's definitely gas, that eggy smell, strongest near the meter cupboards by the stairs.

messages.name: Dwelly Property Team
messages.body: Nadia, please don't use any light switches, door buzzers or lifts, don't smoke, and prop the front door open to ventilate if you can do so safely. If the smell is strong, wait outside. We are treating this as a gas emergency and are acting on it right now.

messages.name: Nadia Ferreira
messages.body: Front door is propped open and I'm out on the pavement with a couple of the other residents. The smell is definitely coming from the meter cupboard area, it's much fainter by the door now it's airing.

messages.name: Dwelly Property Team
messages.body: We've called the National Gas Emergency line on 0800 111 999 and reported a suspected leak at the meter bank - reference given to the operator, an engineer is being dispatched and should be with you within the hour. Please stay clear of the hallway until they arrive. This is now in the gas network's hands and they will make the installation safe.

messages.name: Nadia Ferreira
messages.body: Engineer is here and taping off the meter cupboard. He found the leak straight away, said one of the meter connections was loose. He's capped the supply to that meter and says the smell should clear within the hour. Thanks for moving so quickly on this.

classification.rationale: Suspected gas leak in a communal area - immediate risk to life, escalated to the gas network.

resolution.summary: Suspected gas leak at the communal meter bank reported to the National Gas Emergency line (0800 111 999) within 20 minutes of the first message. Network engineer attended, found a loose meter connection, capped the affected supply and made the installation safe. Repair owned by the gas transporter - outside Dwelly scope.

cases.title: Boiler dead, no heating or hot water

messages.name: Callum Doyle
messages.body: The boiler has completely died overnight - no heating, no hot water, and it's minus two outside. The display is blank, I've checked the fuse spur next to it and that's on. Tried the reset button, nothing. Flat was freezing when we woke up.

messages.name: Dwelly Property Team
messages.body: Callum, sorry about that - no heating in February gets treated as high priority. We're booking Thames & Vale in for you; they're Gas Safe registered so they can open the boiler up. Aiming for first thing tomorrow morning at the latest, today if they can shuffle jobs. If you have plug-in heaters, use them sparingly and not unattended.

messages.name: Thames & Vale Plumbing
messages.body: We can be at Ravensdale Road tomorrow between 8 and 9am. If the display is fully blank it's most likely the PCB fuse or the electrode pack rather than the board itself - we'll bring both. Please confirm access for the morning.

messages.name: Callum Doyle
messages.body: Confirmed, I'll be in from 8. We've dug out an oil radiator for tonight so we'll survive. Please don't let it slip, the flat is properly cold.

messages.name: Thames & Vale Plumbing
messages.body: Boiler is back up. The internal fuse had blown because the ignition electrode lead had chafed and shorted against the casing - replaced the electrode pack and lead, new fuse, cleaned the condensate trap while it was open, fired it up and ran full checks. All safe and heating nicely. £145 invoice to Dwelly.

messages.name: Callum Doyle
messages.body: Radiators are hot and there's hot water again - huge relief, thanks for turning it around in a day. The engineer was in and out in just over an hour.

messages.name: Dwelly Property Team
messages.body: Glad it's sorted, Callum. Closing this one off - the engineer's safety checks all passed, and the annual service later this year will keep an eye on that electrode area. Shout if anything sounds off in the meantime.

classification.rationale: Total loss of heating and hot water in sub-zero weather.

resolution.summary: Shorted ignition electrode lead had blown the boiler's internal fuse; electrode pack, lead and fuse replaced and condensate trap cleaned next morning by Gas Safe engineer, £145.

cases.title: Bathroom extractor fan grinding then stopped

messages.name: Leo Fitzgerald
messages.body: Evening - the extractor fan in the bathroom has been making a horrible grinding noise for about a week, and tonight it ground to a halt mid-shower and now does nothing at all. The bathroom has no window so the mirror stays fogged for ages and the ceiling was dripping with condensation after tonight's shower.

messages.name: Dwelly Property Team
messages.body: Thanks Leo. A dead fan in an internal bathroom needs sorting before damp takes hold, though it's not a same-day emergency. We'll get Bright Spark Electrical booked in this week. In the meantime leave the bathroom door open after showers to let the moisture out.

messages.name: Bright Spark Electrical
messages.body: Hi, Bright Spark here - we can attend Holmleigh Avenue on Tuesday the 17th, morning slot 9-12. We'll need access to the bathroom and the loft hatch on the landing if the ducting runs through there. Please confirm.

messages.name: Leo Fitzgerald
messages.body: Tuesday morning is fine, I'll work from home. The loft hatch is right outside the bathroom door, nothing stored under it. See you then.

messages.name: Bright Spark Electrical
messages.body: Attended this morning. The fan motor bearings have collapsed - it's a 2009 unit and the model is long obsolete, no spares available. The ducting in the loft has also sagged and is holding condensate, which is what killed the motor. Our quote to supply and fit a new continuous-running fan with humidity boost, re-hang the duct on proper supports and make good is £220.

messages.name: Dwelly Property Team
messages.body: Thanks - we've sent the £220 quote over to the landlord for sign-off and will come back to you as soon as we hear.

messages.name: Gerald Ashworth
messages.body: £220 to replace a bathroom fan feels steep to me. Can the existing one not be repaired, or is there a cheaper unit that would do the job? Happy to look at alternatives before committing to that.

messages.name: Dwelly Property Team
messages.body: Understood, Mr Ashworth - we've gone back to Bright Spark for repair feasibility and cheaper options, and we'll set them out for you with pros and cons.

messages.name: Bright Spark Electrical
messages.body: Repair isn't viable - the motor is the failed part and the manufacturer discontinued spares years ago. A basic axial fan would come in around £140 fitted, but it moves roughly half the air and this is a windowless bathroom already showing condensation on the ceiling; it also wouldn't include re-hanging the sagged duct, which will collect water again and take the new motor with it. The £220 unit is sized for an internal bathroom, runs continuously on trickle with humidity boost, and the price includes the duct re-hang and making good.

messages.name: Dwelly Property Team
messages.body: Mr Ashworth - summary as promised: repair is off the table (no spares), and the £140 option is undersized for a bathroom with no window and skips the duct fix, so we'd expect condensation damage and likely a repeat failure. Given the ceiling is already streaking, our recommendation is the £220 installation as the option that actually closes the problem.

messages.name: Gerald Ashworth
messages.body: That's a fair explanation - false economy to fit an undersized fan and leave a sagging duct. Go ahead with the £220 installation, and thank you for pushing back with the detail rather than just re-sending the quote.

messages.name: Bright Spark Electrical
messages.body: Installation complete. New fan fitted and commissioned, running continuous trickle with humidity boost tested against a boiling kettle - kicks up and clears within minutes. Duct re-hung on rigid supports with a fall to the outlet so nothing pools. Ceiling grille made good. Airflow measured and logged for our certificate.

messages.name: Leo Fitzgerald
messages.body: Night and day difference - the mirror actually clears while I'm still in the shower, and it's so quiet I had to check it was on. Thanks for sticking with it through the back-and-forth.

classification.rationale: Failed extraction in a windowless bathroom - damp risk building, but no immediate hazard.

resolution.summary: Obsolete extractor fan with collapsed bearings replaced with a continuous-running humidity-sensing unit and the loft duct re-hung. Landlord initially declined the £220 quote, approved after repair was ruled out and the cheaper option was shown to be undersized for a windowless bathroom.

cases.title: Lights flicker and fuse trips in living room

messages.name: Grace Adeyemi
messages.body: Hi - the living room lights have started flickering, and twice this evening the breaker for that circuit has tripped when I turned the floor lamp on with the TV already running. Second time there was a faint hot plastic smell near the light switch by the door. I've left that circuit switched off at the fuse box for now.

messages.name: Dwelly Property Team
messages.body: Grace, you did exactly the right thing - please keep that circuit off at the consumer unit and don't use the living room sockets or lights until it's been looked at. Flickering plus tripping plus a hot smell points at a loose or arcing connection, which we treat as a safety issue. Bright Spark Electrical will be with you tomorrow morning.

messages.name: Grace Adeyemi
messages.body: Okay, circuit is staying off and we're camped in the kitchen tonight. The smell faded once I switched it off, if that helps. Tomorrow morning works - I leave at 11 so earlier is better.

messages.name: Bright Spark Electrical
messages.body: Attended first thing. Found a loose neutral in the connector block behind the living room light switch - the terminal had never been fully tightened and years of arcing had scorched the block, hence the smell. Replaced the connector block and the switch, re-terminated the wiring, then tested the whole circuit: insulation resistance and earth continuity both fine, no other hot spots. £95 invoice to Dwelly.

messages.name: Grace Adeyemi
messages.body: Everything's back on and rock solid - no flicker with the TV, lamp and hoover all going at once, which was my stress test. Thanks for getting someone out so fast.

messages.name: Dwelly Property Team
messages.body: Great news. The electrician's test results are on file and the rest of the circuit checked out clean, so we're closing this off. As always, any smell of burning from fittings or sockets - switch off first, tell us second.

classification.rationale: Arcing electrical connection with a burning smell - fire safety risk until repaired.

resolution.summary: Loose, arcing neutral behind the living room light switch replaced along with the scorched connector block and switch; full circuit tested clean next morning, £95.

cases.title: Socket by the bed stopped working

messages.name: Sophie Lennox
messages.body: Morning - the double socket on the left side of the bed has stopped working. My phone didn't charge overnight and I thought the charger had died, but the bedside lamp is dead in that socket too and both work fine when I plug them in across the room. Nothing has tripped at the fuse box as far as I can see.

messages.name: Dwelly Property Team
messages.body: Thanks Sophie, that's a helpful bit of detective work - a single dead socket with the rest of the circuit live usually means a failed connection behind that faceplate rather than anything wider. It's electrical, so we'll put Bright Spark Electrical on it rather than have anyone poke around guessing. Please leave that socket unused until they've been. They'll message you directly with a slot.

messages.name: Bright Spark Electrical
messages.body: Visited this morning. The back box terminals on that double socket had worked loose and one conductor had pulled clear - dead socket, but no scorching and the rest of the ring tested healthy. Fitted a new double socket, re-terminated the wiring and tested the full circuit: all readings where they should be. Invoice for £70 going to Dwelly.

messages.name: Dwelly Property Team
messages.body: All sorted then - the electrician confirmed the rest of the circuit tested clean, so this was a one-off loose connection. Closing this off, but do let us know if anything else electrical plays up.

classification.rationale: Single dead socket, no burning smell or tripping - routine electrical fault, book the electrician on a normal slot.

resolution.summary: Loose terminals behind the bedside double socket; socket replaced and circuit tested by Bright Spark Electrical, £70.

messages.name: Marcus Bell
messages.body: Hi, the kitchen sink has been draining slower and slower for about a week and tonight there was still standing water twenty minutes after washing up. I tried a bottle of supermarket unblocker at the weekend and it made no difference. No leaks anywhere, it just won't go down.

messages.name: Dwelly Property Team
messages.body: Thanks Marcus. A week of gradual slowing that shrugs off unblocker usually means a build-up further along the waste pipe rather than in the trap you can reach - so please don't take anything apart yourself. We'll get Thames & Vale Plumbing out to clear it properly. They'll be in touch to arrange access.

messages.name: Thames & Vale Plumbing
messages.body: Hello, Thames & Vale here. We can attend Thursday the 16th between 10 and 12 for the slow-draining sink at Lavender Grove. We'll need access to the kitchen cupboard under the sink. Marcus has confirmed the slot by text, so we're booked in.

messages.name: Thames & Vale Plumbing
messages.body: Job complete. The trap itself was fairly clear but the horizontal waste run to the stack was heavily coated with grease and food deposits - we removed and cleaned the trap, then rodded and flushed the waste run through to the stack. Sink now empties instantly with both bowls full. Invoice for £110 going to Dwelly.

messages.name: Dwelly Property Team
messages.body: Glad that's flowing again, Marcus - closing this one off. One small ask from the plumber: let cooking fat cool and bin it rather than rinsing it down, as that waste run has a long flat stretch that catches grease. Anything else, you know where we are.

classification.rationale: Sink still usable but deteriorating; blockage needs a plumber on a routine slot before it becomes a full stoppage.

resolution.summary: Grease build-up in the kitchen waste run cleared by rodding and flushing; trap cleaned, drainage restored, £110.

cases.title: Upstairs neighbours stomping at 2am every night

messages.name: Aisha Rahman
messages.body: It's ten past two in the morning and the people upstairs are stomping around again - it sounds like furniture being dragged and someone pacing in boots. This has been happening most nights for about three weeks now and I'm barely sleeping. Can you please do something about it?

messages.name: Dwelly Property Team
messages.body: Aisha, I'm sorry - three weeks of broken sleep is miserable and I completely understand you reaching for any channel at 2am. So we know what we're dealing with: is the noise coming from the flat directly above you, and have you had a chance to speak to the people up there about it?

messages.name: Aisha Rahman
messages.body: Yes, it's definitely the flat directly above. I put a polite note through their door last week and nothing changed. Honestly at this point could you send someone to put soundproofing in the ceiling? I'll take anything.

messages.name: Dwelly Property Team
messages.body: I want to be straight with you about what we can and can't do here. There's nothing broken or faulty in the building - the floors and ceilings are as they were built - so this isn't something we can send a contractor out for, and retrofitting soundproofing isn't a repair we're able to raise. What does help with neighbour noise: keep a simple diary of dates and times, try speaking to them in person rather than a note if you feel comfortable, and if it carries on, the council's environmental health team deals with persistent night-time noise and takes diaries like yours seriously. One thing we can do from our side: that flat is also managed by us, so we can pass on a polite general reminder about night-time noise.

messages.name: Aisha Rahman
messages.body: That's fair enough, I did wonder if I was asking the wrong people. Yes please do send the reminder - and I've started a note on my phone logging the times. If it's still going in a couple of weeks I'll contact the council like you suggest.

messages.name: Dwelly Property Team
messages.body: Done - a courtesy reminder about night-time noise went to the upstairs household this morning, without naming you. I'm going to close this report now since there's no repair for us to carry out, but that doesn't mean we've stopped caring: if anything building-related ever comes up, or you need us to confirm your reports to the council, message us any time.

classification.rationale: No fault with the property itself - neighbour noise is a tenancy and communication matter, not a repair we can raise.

resolution.summary: Night-time noise from the upstairs flat; nothing in the building to repair. Tenant guided towards a noise diary and the council's environmental health route, courtesy reminder sent to the upstairs household, report closed without works.

cases.title: Ground-floor window latch broken, won't lock

messages.name: Ellie Cartwright
messages.body: Hi, the latch on the living room window has snapped - the handle just spins and the window won't lock at all. We're on the ground floor and it faces straight onto the street. I can push it shut but anyone could pull it open from outside. I'm out at work all day tomorrow and honestly a bit worried about leaving it like this.

messages.name: Dwelly Property Team
messages.body: Ellie, understood - a ground-floor window that won't lock isn't something we'll leave sitting in the queue. We're arranging a locksmith for first thing tomorrow morning before you leave for work. For tonight: wedge the window firmly shut from the inside (a folded piece of card or a rubber doorstop jammed in the frame works), keep the curtains closed, and don't leave anything valuable in view of it.

messages.name: SecureFit Locks
messages.body: Evening, SecureFit Locks here - Dwelly has asked us to attend 3 Herrick Court. We can be with you at 8am tomorrow, before you head out. It looks like a standard espag handle failure from the description; we carry stock so it should be a single visit. Someone will need to let us in.

messages.name: SecureFit Locks
messages.body: Attended at 8 as arranged. The gearbox inside the espag handle had stripped, which is why the handle was spinning free. Fitted a new key-locking handle and checked the espagnolette rods engage properly at all three keeps - window now closes tight and locks with the key. Two keys left with the tenant. Invoice for £60 going to Dwelly.

messages.name: Ellie Cartwright
messages.body: They were done before I left for work - window locks properly and actually shuts tighter than it did before. Thank you for turning that around overnight, I'll sleep a lot better.

classification.rationale: Ground-floor window facing the street that cannot be locked - the flat is unsecured until it's fixed.

resolution.summary: Stripped espag handle gearbox on a street-facing ground-floor window; locksmith fitted a new key-locking handle next morning, window secure, £60.

cases.title: Black mould spots in bedroom corner

messages.name: Rachel Nguyen
messages.body: Hi, I've found black mould spots in the corner of the bedroom where the outside wall meets the ceiling. I wiped them off with mould spray two weeks ago and they've come back in the same spot, slightly bigger. It's the corner behind the wardrobe. Should I be worried there's a leak?

messages.name: Dwelly Property Team
messages.body: Thanks Rachel - you're right to flag it coming back, that's the important detail. Mould in an external corner is either water getting in from somewhere or condensation, and they need completely different fixes, so we want to find out which before anyone reaches for paint. Could you send photos of the corner, and tell us: do you get water droplets on the bedroom windows in the mornings, and is anything dried indoors in that room?

messages.name: Rachel Nguyen
messages.body: Photos attached. And yes to both actually - the bedroom window is streaming most mornings this winter, and I dry laundry on an airer next to the radiator in there because there's nowhere else. The wall in that corner feels cold and slightly damp to the touch.

messages.name: Dwelly Property Team
messages.body: That's useful. The wet windows point one way, but the flat above yours has a bathroom over that corner, so we're not going to guess - we've booked Thames & Vale Plumbing to inspect for any leak in the pipework or from above before anything else. They'll take moisture readings across that wall too. Please pull the wardrobe out from the corner before the visit if you can.

messages.name: Thames & Vale Plumbing
messages.body: Inspection done at Penrose Avenue. We checked the bathroom above - traps, seals and visible pipe runs are all dry - and took moisture readings across the bedroom wall. Readings are highest at the surface and drop off with depth, which is the signature of condensation, not a leak. The corner is a cold spot: external wall on two sides, air trapped behind the wardrobe. No repair works needed from us. Invoice for the inspection, £90, going to Dwelly.

messages.name: Dwelly Property Team
messages.body: So the good news is nothing is leaking, Rachel - the cause is condensation settling in that cold corner. What will actually keep it away: leave a hand's width of gap between the wardrobe and the wall, keep the window trickle vent open, crack the window while laundry is drying in there (that airer is putting litres of water into the air), and keep the bedroom door open during the day so air moves through. Treat the existing spots once more with the mould spray - they should not return if the moisture drops. We'll check in with you in a couple of weeks.

messages.name: Rachel Nguyen
messages.body: Quick update - wardrobe moved out from the wall, trickle vent open, and I've been cracking the window on laundry days. The windows are noticeably drier in the mornings and the corner has stayed clear since I treated it. Looks like that was it.

messages.name: Dwelly Property Team
messages.body: That's exactly what we hoped to hear - two weeks clear with drier mornings means the ventilation changes are doing the work. We're closing this one off. If the spots ever come back despite all that, tell us straight away, because then it would be worth a second look at the wall itself.

classification.rationale: Recurring mould needs the cause found promptly, but no active leak reported - inspect before treating.

resolution.summary: Leak inspection found pipework above dry and moisture readings consistent with condensation in a cold external corner; ventilation guidance given, mould treated and not returned after two weeks, £90 inspection.

cases.title: Radiator in the small bedroom stays cold

messages.name: Josh Palmer
messages.body: Evening - the radiator in the small bedroom stays cold when the heating is on. All the other radiators in the flat get properly hot. This one is warm-ish at the bottom but stone cold across the top. The valve on the side is fully open as far as I can tell.

messages.name: Dwelly Property Team
messages.body: Thanks Josh - warm at the bottom and cold across the top is the classic sign of air trapped in the radiator, and it's a two-minute fix you can safely do yourself. You'll need a radiator key - there should be one in the kitchen odds-and-ends drawer, or any hardware shop has them for a pound or two. Then: turn the heating off and let the radiators cool, put a cloth under the small square valve at the top corner of the radiator, and turn it a quarter-turn anticlockwise with the key. You'll hear a hiss - that's the air escaping. The moment water starts to dribble out instead, close it back up snugly. That's it.

messages.name: Josh Palmer
messages.body: Well that was oddly satisfying - found the key in the drawer, long hiss, little spurt of water, closed it up. Heating back on and the radiator is now hot top to bottom for the first time this winter. Thanks for talking me through it.

messages.name: Dwelly Property Team
messages.body: Perfect. One last thing: have a quick look at the pressure gauge on the front of the boiler - bleeding a radiator can nudge it down, and if the needle has dropped below 1 bar, the filling loop instructions are on the inside cover of the boiler manual in the hallway cupboard. If the same radiator goes cold again within a few weeks, tell us, as air coming back usually means the system needs a proper look. Closing this one off - nice work.

classification.rationale: One radiator underperforming with the rest of the heating working - no urgency, likely resolvable with guidance.

resolution.summary: Trapped air in the small bedroom radiator; tenant bled it themselves following step-by-step guidance, radiator fully hot, no callout raised.

cases.title: Washing machine leaks during spin cycle

messages.name: Chloe Sanders
messages.body: Hi, the washing machine has started leaking - a puddle creeps out from underneath it during the spin cycle, maybe half a mug of water each wash. I've been putting a towel down. Quick question though: the machine was here when I moved in, so is this one for you or is it my appliance to fix?

messages.name: Dwelly Property Team
messages.body: Good question, Chloe, and easy answer: the machine is listed on your inventory as supplied with the flat, so it's the landlord's to keep in working order - nothing for you to arrange or pay. Please stop using it until it's looked at though; a spin-cycle leak can go from half a mug to a flooded kitchen floor without warning, and the flat below yours would feel that. We'll check with the landlord and get a plumber booked.

messages.name: Alan Pemberton
messages.body: Fine to go ahead - the machine came with the flat and it's only a few years old, so repair rather than replace if it's economical. Send someone whenever suits Chloe and keep me posted on the cost.

messages.name: Dan Whitfield (FlowFix Plumbing Ltd)
messages.body: Attended this afternoon. Ran the machine on a rinse and spin with the plinth off: the door seal has a split at the bottom fold - water sits there and gets flung past the seal at high spin speed. Hoses, pump and connections all sound. Fitted a new door seal, ran a full hot cycle and a max spin: bone dry underneath. Invoice for £120 to Dwelly.

messages.name: Chloe Sanders
messages.body: Two loads done since the repair and the floor is completely dry - towel officially retired. Thanks for sorting it so quickly, and good to know whose job these things are for next time.

messages.name: Dwelly Property Team
messages.body: Glad it's behaving, Chloe. The £120 has gone to Alan as it's a supplied appliance, and the plumber's notes are on file. Closing this one off - and yes, anything that was in the flat when you moved in, flag it to us first and we'll take it from there.

classification.rationale: Contained leak from an appliance during use - repairable on a routine slot, machine out of use meanwhile.

resolution.summary: Split door seal on the landlord-supplied washing machine replaced by FlowFix; test cycles dry, cost passed to the landlord, £120.
